1.1: Sha’ul, an emissary of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ by the desire of Elohim, according to the promise of ḥai which is in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏,
1.2: to Timotiyos, my beloved son: Favor, compassion, peace from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Father, and Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 our Aḏon.
1.3: I thank Elohim, whom I serve with a clear conscience, as my forefathers did, as I unceasingly remember you in my prayers night and day,
1.4: longing to see you, as I remember your tears, so that I might be filled with joy.
1.5: For I recollect the sincere belief which is in you, which dwelt first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunikĕ, and I am persuaded is in you too.
1.6: For this reason I remind you to stir up the gift of Elohim which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
1.7: For Elohim has not given us a spirit of cowardice, but of power and of love and of self-control.
1.8: So do not be ashamed of the witness of our Aḏon, nor of me His prisoner, but suffer hardship with me for the Good News according to the power of Elohim,
1.9: who has saved us and called us with a qodesh calling, not according to our works, but according to His own purpose and favor which was given to us in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 before times of old,
1.10: but now revealed by the appearing of our Savior 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, who indeed abolished death and brought ḥai and incorruptibility to light through the Good News,
1.11: for which I was appointed a proclaimer, and an emissary, and a teacher of the gentiles.
1.12: For this reason I also suffer these, but I am not ashamed, for I know whom I have believed and am persuaded that He is able to watch over that which I have entrusted to Him until that Day.
1.13: Hold the pattern of sound words which you have heard from me, in belief and love which are in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
1.14: Watch over the good deposit that was entrusted to you, by the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh dwelling in us.
1.15: You know this, that all those in Asia have turned away from me, among whom are Phugellos and Hermogenĕs.
1.16: The Aḏon grant compassion unto the household of Onĕsiphoros, for he often refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain,
1.17: but when he was in Rome, he eagerly searched for me and found me.
1.18: The Aḏon grant to him to find compassion from the Aḏon in that Day. And you know very well how many ways he attended to me at Ephesos.

2.1: You then, my son, be strong in the favor that is in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
2.2: And what you have heard from me among many witnesses, entrust these to trustworthy men who shall be competent to teach others as well.
2.3: Suffer hardship as a good soldier of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ.
2.4: No one serving as a soldier gets involved in the affairs of this life, in order to please him who enlisted him as a soldier.
2.5: And if anyone competes in a game, he is not crowned unless he competes according to the rules.
2.6: The hard-working farmer ought to be first to receive his share of the crops.
2.7: Think over what I say, for the Aḏon shall give you understanding into all this.
2.8: Remember that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, of the seed of Dawiḏ, was raised from the dead according to my Good News,
2.9: for which I suffer hardship, as a criminal, unto chains, but the Word of Elohim is not chained.
2.10: So I endure through it all for the sake of the chosen, so that they too obtain deliverance which is in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 with everlasting esteem.
2.11: Trustworthy is the word: For if we died with Him, we shall also live with Him.
2.12: If we endure, we shall also reign with Him. If we deny, He also shall deny us.
2.13: If we are not trustworthy, He remains trustworthy, it is impossible for Him to deny Himself.
2.14: Remind them of this, earnestly witnessing before the Aḏon, not to wage verbal battles - which is useless - to the overthrowing of the hearers.
2.15: Do your utmost to present yourself approved to Elohim, a worker who does not need to be ashamed, rightly handling the Word of Truth.
2.16: But keep away from profane, empty babblings, for they go on to more wickedness,
2.17: and their word shall eat its way like gangrene. Humenaios and Philĕtos are of this sort,
2.18: who have missed concerning the truth, saying that the resurrection has already taken place, and overthrow the belief of some.
2.19: However, the solid foundation of Elohim stands firm, having this seal, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 knows those who are His,” and, “Let everyone who names the Name of Mashiaḥ turn away from unrighteousness.”
2.20: But in a large house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay, some unto value and some unto no value.
2.21: If, then, anyone cleanses himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto value, having been qodesh, of good use to the Aḏon, having been prepared for every good work.
2.22: And flee from the lusts of youth, but pursue righteousness, belief, love, peace with those calling on the Aḏon out of a clean heart.
2.23: But refuse foolish and stupid questions, knowing that they breed quarrels.
2.24: And a servant of the Aḏon should not quarrel but be gentle towards all, able to teach, patient when wronged,
2.25: in meekness instructing those who are in opposition, if perhaps Elohim may give them repentance unto a thorough knowledge of the truth,
2.26: and they come to their senses, out of the snare of the devil, having been taken captive by him to do his desire.

3.1: But know this, that in the last days hard times shall come.
3.2: For men shall be lovers of self, lovers of money, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, thankless, wrong-doers,
3.3: unloving, unforgiving, slanderers, without self-control, fierce, haters of good,
3.4: betrayers, reckless, puffed up, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of Elohim,
3.5: having a form of reverence but denying its power. And turn away from these!
3.6: For among them are those who creep into households and captivate silly women loaded down with sins, led away by various lusts,
3.7: always learning and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth.
3.8: And as Yoḥane and Mamrĕ opposed Mosheh, so do these also oppose the truth - men of corrupt minds, found worthless concerning the belief;
3.9: but they shall not go on further, for their folly shall be obvious to all, as also that of those men became.
3.10: But you closely followed my teaching, the Way of ḥai, the purpose, the belief, the patience, the love, the endurance,
3.11: the persecutions, the sufferings, which came to me at Antioḵeia, at Ikonion, at Lustra - what persecutions I bore. Yet out of them all the Aḏon delivered me.
3.12: And indeed, all those wanting to live reverently in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, shall be persecuted.
3.13: But evil men and impostors shall go on to the worse, leading astray and being led astray.
3.14: But you, stay in what you have learned and trusted, having known from whom you have learned,
3.15: and that from a child you have known the Qodesh Scriptures, which are able to make you wise for deliverance through belief in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
3.16: All Scripture is breathed by Elohim and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for straightening, for instruction in righteousness,
3.17: that the man of Elohim might be fitted, equipped for every good work.

4.1: In the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, who shall judge the living and the dead at His appearing and His Malḵuth, I earnestly charge you:
4.2: Proclaim the Word! Be urgent in season, out of season. Reprove, warn, appeal, with all patience and teaching.
4.3: For there shall be a time when they shall not bear sound teaching, but according to their own desires, having itching ears, they shall heap up for themselves teachers,
4.4: and they shall indeed turn their ears away from the truth, and be turned aside to myths.
4.5: But you be sober in all, suffer hardships, do the work of an evangelist, accomplish your service completely.
4.6: For I am already being poured out, and the time of my departure has arrived.
4.7: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have guarded the belief.
4.8: For the rest, there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Aḏon, the righteous Judge, shall give to me on that Day, and not to me only but also to all those loving His appearing.
4.9: Do your best to come to me soon,
4.10: for Dĕmas, having loved this present world, has deserted me and went to Thessalonikĕ, Krĕskĕs to Galatia, Titos to Dalmatia.
4.11: Lukas alone is with me. Take Markos and bring him with you, for he is of good use to me for service.
4.12: And Tuḵikos I have sent to Ephesos.
4.13: Bring the cloak that I left with Karpos at Troas when you come, and the books, especially the parchments.
4.14: Alexandros the coppersmith did many evils to me. The Aḏon shall repay him according to his works.
4.15: You, too, beware of him, for he strongly opposed our words.
4.16: At my first defense no one stood with me, but all forsook me. Let it not be held against them.
4.17: But the Aḏon stood with me and strengthened me, so that through me the preaching might be completely accomplished, and that all the gentiles should hear. And I was rescued out of the lion’s mouth.
4.18: And the Aḏon shall rescue me from every wicked work and save me for His Malḵuth of the shamayim. To Him be esteem forever and ever. Amĕn!
4.19: Greet Priska and Aqulas, and the house of Onĕsiphoros.
4.20: Ĕrastos stayed in Qorinth, but I left Trophimos sick in Milĕtos.
4.21: Do your best to come before winter. Eubulos greets you, and Pudĕs, and Linos, and Klaudia, and all the brothers.
4.22: The Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ be with your spirit. Favor be with you. Amĕn.
